title: A counterexample to the Etzion-Silberstein conjecture
summary: The Etzion-Silberstein conjecture asserts that the Singleton-type upper bound for linear Ferrers-diagram rank-metric codes is attained for every Ferrers diagram, minimum rank distance, and finite field. Let $E$ be the Ferrers diagram with column heights $(5,5,5,5,1,1)$. The bound for minimum rank distance $3$ is $12$. We prove that every binary linear code supported on $E$ with minimum rank distance $3$ has dimension at most $11$, and we give an explicit code of dimension $11$.
